questions.q: Ethyl acetate is treated with sodium ethoxide and then with dilute acid. The product is:
questions.explain: The tetrahedral intermediate expels C₂H₅O⁻ instead of being protonated, so the product is a β-keto ester, not the β-hydroxy compound an aldol would give.

questions.q: Which base is the best choice for the Claisen self-condensation of ethyl propanoate?
questions.explain: The alkoxide should match the ester's alkoxy group so that any attack on the carbonyl simply regenerates the same ester. NaOMe would cause transesterification, and NaOH would saponify the ester.

questions.q: Which ester does NOT give a good Claisen self-condensation product with sodium ethoxide?
questions.explain: Ethyl 2-methylpropanoate has only one α-H. It is used up making the enolate, so the β-keto ester formed has no acidic CH between its carbonyls to be deprotonated, and that final deprotonation is what drives the reaction.

questions.q: Cyclohexanone and ethyl acetate are treated with sodium ethoxide, then with H₃O⁺. The main product is:
questions.explain: The ketone α-H is more acidic than the ester α-H, so cyclohexanone forms the enolate and ethyl acetate is the acceptor, losing EtO⁻ to give the β-diketone. Ethyl 2-oxocyclohexanecarboxylate would need the roles reversed.
